Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible.

A public building shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and any other facility that makes them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 4]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3]. This right of access to public premises guarantees a person with disability a right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Factsheet Section 3]. This provision is further complemented by sections 4 and 5 of the Bill that require public facilities to be accessible and usable by persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 3]. Public facilities include road-side walks, pedestrian crossings and special facilities such as elevators, crutches, guide canes, toilet facilities, door protective and re-opening devices [Factsheet Section 3].

Before erecting any public structure, its plan shall be scrutinised by the relevant authority to ensure it conforms with the building code [Act cl. 7]. A government or government agency, body or individual responsible for the approval of building plans shall not approve the plan of a public building if it does not make provision for accessibility facilities in line with the building code [Act cl. 7]. Officers who approve such a plan commit an offence and are liable on conviction to a fine of at least N1,000,000 or a two-year imprisonment term or both [Factsheet Section 7,8].

All public buildings or structures, whether immovable or not, must be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs, within a five-year transitory period [Factsheet Section 6].

Yes, the Act covers access to vehicles and transport.

Government transport service providers are mandated to provide lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops for persons with disabilities, including those using wheelchairs [Act cl. 10]. Every public vehicle must also have functional audible and visual displays of their destination within five years from the commencement of this Act [Act cl. 10].

Transport service providers shall make provisions for lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 11]. Lifts, ramps, and all other accessibility equipment in or for vehicles, and at parks or bus stops, shall be maintained in operational condition [Act cl. 11]. There shall be regular and frequent maintenance of all accessibility aids and equipment, and defective ones shall be promptly repaired or replaced [Act cl. 11]. Before a person with disability boards or alights from a vehicle, the driver must ensure that the vehicle comes to a stop [Act cl. 11]. When a person with disability intends to board a vehicle, all other intending passengers shall wait for them to board before them [Act cl. 11]. These provisions are also summarized in the factsheet, which states that Section 10 mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps, and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks, and bus stops to persons with disabilities, and every public vehicle to have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years of commencement of this Act [Factsheet Section 10,11]. A similar provision to section 10(1) is provided in section 11 for all transport service providers [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Section 11 also mandates the regular and frequent maintenance of accessibility aids and equipment in vehicles [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Additionally, section 11(4) places a duty of care on a driver who must ensure that his vehicle comes to a stop before a person with disability alights from the vehicle [Factsheet Section 10,11]. There is also a responsibility placed on all intending passengers to wait for a person with disability to board before them in section 11(5) [Factsheet Section 10,11].
